['When light travels from one medium to another, its speed can change because the properties of the two media, such as their density and refractive index, can be different. Similarly, when light encounters a boundary between two media, it might have to change direction to follow the boundary. The amount that the light ray bends depends on the angle at which it hits the boundary and the difference in the refractive indices of the two media. When the refractive index is higher in the second medium, the light ray will bend towards the normal (a line perpendicular to the boundary). When the refractive index is lower in the second medium, the light ray will bend away from the normal. I hope this helps to explain why the direction of the light ray can change when it travels from one medium to another. Let me know if you have any more questions!']
